marks.q: As such, subject to no further unexpected events, the Group now expects full year operating profit to be in the region of £165m.
Given the strength of our performance in December, we now expect 2021 full year operating profit to be marginally in excess of our previous guidance of in the region of £165m.
However, we have a flexible and highly diversified business model which allows us to adapt quickly to changing market conditions.
We are pleased with the Group's performance in Q1 and, at this early stage in the year, expect 2022 operating profit to be slightly ahead of company compiled consensus of £202m.
We are pleased with the Group's performance in the first half of the year and currently expect 2022 full year operating profit to be in line with company compiled consensus of £205m.
However, at this point, our expectations for 2022 full year operating profit remain in line with the company compiled consensus of £206m .
We are pleased with the Group's performance in Q3, and currently expect 2022 full year operating profit to be in line with company compiled consensus of £204m.
Given the slowdown in trading towards the end of Q4, we now expect 2022 full year operating profit to be c. £195m.

Given our highly diversified and adaptable business model, with a variable cost base and a strong balance sheet, we believe we are well-positioned to weather the uncertainty and continue to deliver strong shareholder returns.

The challenging conditions we saw towards the end of 2022 continued into 2023, with lower levels of both candidate and client confidence resulting in delays in decision making and candidates being more reluctant to accept offers.
At this stage of the year, the Board expects 2023 operating profit to be in line with company compiled consensus of £137.6m.
However, against this backdrop, we continue to see candidate shortages and good levels of vacancies, as well as continued high fee rates.
At this stage of the year, the Board expects 2023 operating profit, excluding the previously announced one off cost of c. £5m, to be between £125m - £130m.
Despite the year-on-year decline in gross profit, we are still seeing good activity levels, albeit we did see a deterioration in job flow through Q4.

We saw a slower end to 2023 due to macro uncertainty impacting candidate and client sentiment, which has continued into January and February, albeit they are two of the smallest months of the year from a trading perspective.

Conversion of final interviews to accepted offers is still the most significant challenge, as candidate and client sentiment remains subdued reflecting the general macro-economic uncertainty in most of our markets.

Given the weaker than expected trading in June, recent increased geopolitical and macro-economic uncertainty and consequently a more cautious view for H2, the Board now expects full year 2024 operating profit to be in the region of £60m.

Given the Group's fundamental strengths, we believe we will continue to perform well despite the challenging environment, and we are confident in our ability to implement our strategy driving the long-term profitability of the Group.
We continued to see challenging market conditions throughout the Group in Q3, with no improvement in September after the seasonally quieter summer months.

Market conditions remained challenging in Q4 and whilst most markets were sequentially stable, we experienced a further worsening in Europe, particularly in our two largest markets, France and Germany.
We saw a slower end to 2024, which has continued into January and February, albeit they are two of the smallest months of the year from a trading perspective.

Despite the uncertain outlook due to the increasingly unpredictable economic environment, PageGroup has a highly diversified and adaptable business model, a strong balance sheet and our cost base is under continuous review.
We saw a slight deterioration in activity levels and trading in Continental Europe, particularly in our two largest markets, France and Germany.
The Board continues to expect 2025 Operating Profit to be broadly in line with current market consensus of c. £22m
We continued to experience subdued levels of sentiment and confidence in Europe, particularly in our two largest markets, France and Germany, as well as in the UK.
However, we continued to experience lower levels of confidence in Europe, particularly in France, our largest market, as well as in the UK.
However, we continued to grow in the US, and we saw improved conditions in Asia Pacific, particularly during the second half of the year.
Despite this market outlook, we continue to focus on controlling the controllables, invest in innovation and technology, and remain confident in the execution of our strategy.
Whilst we have seen improvement and signs of a normalisation in trading in a number of our markets, there remains a high degree of uncertainty in the outlook for the rest of the year.
